notes: Seventh sweep (previous sweep d04061d): five skill runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier, each result.json recording head 0814e8d with no uncommitted changes and skill_hash 38869366..., which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the current idiomatic-elixir/ folder; every transcript contains the new Readability text ("A line break is not decomposition"). skills_listed is 209 for every run. Opus-1 read SKILL.md and references/library-design.md with Read, haiku-2 SKILL.md with cat and library-design.md with sed (the whole 84-line file), and haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 SKILL.md only, so Expected reads (none) is met in all five. Opus-1 and haiku-2 also wrote probe files under /tmp outside their run folders, which no rule covers. In the scratch folder all five pass mix format --check-formatted and run against a stand-in Decimal written there (the earlier graders' stub plus nan?/1 and inf?/1, which opus-1 calls). A probe gave correct per-currency totals (haiku-1 in integer cents, 2000 for 19.99 + 0.01), correct last-order values and empty results for []; every run returns {:error, ...} for a missing key, a bad amount, an unknown status and a bad date, and haiku-2 raises FunctionClauseError for a non-string amount because string_field/2 (lines 156-161) does not check the value's type, which no listed rule covers. Haiku-1 and haiku-2 report the last order as a DateTime (last_order_at) where the prompt asks for a date, which no rule covers.

Rules changed since d04061d, graded against the current text. The with rule is decided by "One step is a `with` only when its body cannot fail and there is no `else`" (build/1 in all five: opus-1 66-68, haiku-1 25-27, haiku-2 72-74, sonnet-1 75-77, sonnet-2 64-68) and by "A body that is one call whose `{:ok, value}` or `{:error, reason}` goes out as the function's own result ... is a tail call, not a second step, and the one-step `with` stays" (haiku-2 130-132, sonnet-1 85-87); under the d04061d text ("With one there is nothing to chain ... so use `case`") every one of these would have been a violation, and all five 2026-10-23 runs wrote build/1 as a case. The pass-through sentence ("A `case` whose error clause is `{:error, _reason} = error -> error` ... write it as the `with`") finds no such case: opus-1 (76-82) and sonnet-2 (109-115) retag the error with the row position, and haiku-1's reduce_while case (32-35) wraps it in {:halt, error}. The captures rule's new fn paragraph, "A `fn` body is laid out like any other body: one expression stays on the head's line", makes the one-line Enum.sort_by(fn {customer_id, count} -> {-count, customer_id} end) that all five runs write clean; the 2026-10-31-check text ("A `fn` that binds names takes the room its names earn") graded the same line violated, and the d04061d text held it clean (2026-10-23 opus-1 line 228). Its other new sentence, "with `&1` and `&2` in that order and each used once", is met by &Decimal.add(&1.amount, &2) (haiku-2 108, sonnet-1 167). The do: rule's new text ("a literal, a tuple, a field read, a comparison, or a call, nested or not"; the capture, one-line if and for sentences) adds no violation: haiku-2's defp completed(orders), do: Enum.filter(orders, &(&1.status == :completed)) (line 125) holds a capture of a comparison, not "a capture that carries a call with arguments of its own", held clean as 2026-10-30-check-3 held the identical line; opus-1's two ifs (183, 192) are blocks; no run writes for. The Enum/Map table's two new rows (List.keymember?/3, for as a filter) have no matching shape in any run; the unchanged sentence "a `reduce` that reads and writes one key per element is these two written by hand" decides, 0 of 5.

Rules new to this case's row since 2026-10-23 (no earlier sweep standard here). Write pipelines that start with a value and read top to bottom: decided by "A pipeline never sits on one line, however short"; haiku-2 line 94 (totals: customer_orders |> completed() |> totals_by_currency(),) is the one violation, 1 of 5; the d04061d text ("then one transformation per line") would also have counted it. Inline `->` clauses that read at a glance; otherwise put each body on its own line (the d04061d skill had no `->` rule; the 2026-10-23 order-report grades graded none): clean in all five, decided by "stays on one line when the clauses form a table, or when each body is one expression simple enough to take in together with its pattern" and "a clause whose pattern, `->` and body pass about 70 characters after the indentation goes to two lines"; the longest one-line case clause is opus-1 line 162 at exactly 70 characters, and the longest single-clause fn arguments (opus-1 99, haiku-1 112) have a 71-character clause holding one tuple, held within "about 70" under "A single-clause `fn` passed as an argument reads the same way: one expression stays on its line"; every case with a clause of several expressions or a nested call (opus-1 169-178, haiku-1 69-79, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 throughout) breaks every clause with blank lines between. One expression per line, and tabular clauses: clean in all five, decided by "A line reads in one pass when it holds a selection and the one expression that selection produces" and the table paragraph (parse_status/1 in every run); the one-line sort_by fns are covered by "`fn {customer_id, count} -> {-count, customer_id} end` holds a pattern and one expression and stays on one line". Name a step instead of wrapping an expression: clean in all five, decided by "A binding earns its place when it names a recognizable thing or a stage of the computation"; the sonnet runs' formatter-wrapped {:ok, %Order{...}} (sonnet-1 103-110, sonnet-2 149-156) is held clean as in both 2026-10-31 check batches, a tag around a struct literal with no computational steps to name, and sonnet-1's 92-column line 167 is one expression on one line, under "Length alone decides nothing".

Unchanged rules, graded to the 2026-10-23 standard. Atoms, dates, money and processes: clean in all five (haiku-1 stores integer cents, the others Decimal; every run uses Enum.max(DateTime) or Enum.max_by(..., DateTime)). Lists: haiku-1 prepends in reduce_while without reversing (line 33), held clean as before because nothing downstream depends on the order; the others prepend and reverse. Naming: haiku-1's defp fetch_string(row, key) (line 60), which returns {:error, {:invalid_field, key}} or {:error, {:missing_field, key}}, breaks "A function that looks a key up and also checks the value, returning `{:error, reason}`, is not a `fetch`", the shape the 2026-10-23 baseline opus-1 grade counted (fetch_string/2); 1 of 5. Other rules: haiku-1's @doc on build/1 (lines 10-23) has no ## Examples, recorded under other_violations as in earlier sweeps; sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 match the five required keys in a multi-line head with a catch-all clause below (sonnet-1 90-114, sonnet-2 136-160), held clean under the head rule as the 2026-10-23 grades held haiku-1 and sonnet-2. No case or with nests inside another, every defstruct uses @enforce_keys, and no other violation was found.
